reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Pseudopalisading necrosis plus microvascular proliferation equals glioblastoma grade 4
Child posterior fossa tumour with CSF seeding means medulloblastoma
Dural tail plus whorls and psammoma bodies mean meningioma
Bitemporal hemianopia localises to pituitary chiasm compression
reference.pathophysiology: Gliomas infiltrate along white matter tracts beyond imaging margins through accumulated IDH, cell cycle and growth pathway mutations, while extra axial tumours compress from outside. Embryonal childhood tumours arise from developmental progenitors with pathway mutations (hedgehog, WNT) determining medulloblastoma groups and prognosis.
additionalDifferentials: Glioblastoma versus metastasis versus lymphoma ring lesions
Meningioma versus schwannoma extra axial tumours
Medulloblastoma versus pilocytic astrocytoma in children
additionalInvestigations: MRI with contrast and spectroscopy patterns
Histology with IDH and molecular glioma profiling
Staging spine MRI and CSF cytology for embryonal tumours
